KYC data, ownership records, screening results, approvals, review dates and supporting documents lose context when they live in separate tools. Duevio keeps the operational record connected.

Privacy Notice

This Privacy Notice explains how Duevio collects and processes personal data in connection with the Duevio website, online signup, demo and Custom enquiries, account administration and related commercial communications.

It does not govern personal data processed by Duevio on behalf of Customers through the Duevio Platform. That processing is addressed separately under the Duevio Data Processing Agreement.

1. Who we are

For the processing described in this Privacy Notice, Duevio acts as the data controller.

2. Scope of this Notice

This Privacy Notice applies to personal data collected through:

Where you access Duevio because an organisation has invited you to provide KYC, onboarding or other information through a secure Duevio link, that organisation will normally be the controller of the information you provide and Duevio will process that information on its behalf.

In that situation, you should refer to the privacy notice of the organisation that invited you.

Contact and professional information: such as your name, work email address, organisation, role and contact details.

Organisation and commercial information: such as organisation type, jurisdiction, operating jurisdictions, team size, selected plan, implementation requirements and information you provide when requesting a demo or Custom consultation.

Account information: such as your username, account identifier, authentication information, account status and preferences.

Communications: including enquiries, demo requests, support communications and other information you choose to provide to us.

Subscription and transaction information: such as the plan purchased, transaction status, invoice details and payment references.

Technical and security information: such as IP address, browser or device information, login records, timestamps, security events and information reasonably required to protect the website and Services.

Cookie and preference information: where applicable, including consent choices, language preferences and analytics information where you have consented to non-essential technologies.

Duevio does not normally receive or store your complete payment-card or PayPal credentials where payment is processed directly by the applicable payment provider.

4. Why we process personal data

Service, security, contractual and administrative communications are not marketing communications and may continue where necessary in connection with your account or Subscription.

6. Customer Data processed through Duevio

Duevio Customers may use the Platform to process information concerning their own clients, prospective clients, beneficial owners, directors, representatives and other individuals.

For such Customer Personal Data, the relevant Customer ordinarily determines why and how the information is processed and acts as controller, while Duevio acts as processor or, where appropriate, subprocessor.

That processing is governed by the agreement between Duevio and the Customer, including the Duevio Data Processing Agreement.

This Privacy Notice does not change those respective roles.

7. Who receives personal data

Personal data may be accessed by authorised Duevio personnel and by service providers used to operate the website and Services.

Depending on the relevant service, recipients may include providers of:

  • cloud hosting and infrastructure;
  • email and communications;
  • payment processing;
  • website analytics and consent management;
  • security and technical services;
  • professional, accounting or legal services; and
  • other services reasonably necessary to operate Duevio.

Duevio's core infrastructure is hosted within the European Union and includes infrastructure provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS) and infrastructure owned or controlled directly by Duevio.

Duevio may also disclose personal data where required by a competent court, regulator, supervisory authority or other public authority in accordance with applicable law.

Duevio does not sell personal data.

8. Payments

Payments may be processed by third-party payment providers.

Where you are redirected to a payment provider, that provider may process payment-card, PayPal or other payment information under its own privacy terms and legal responsibilities.

Duevio receives only the information reasonably required to confirm and administer the transaction, such as payment status, amount, transaction reference and billing information.

9. International transfers

Duevio configures its core production infrastructure and relevant services for processing within the European Union.

If personal data is transferred outside the European Economic Area in the future, Duevio will ensure that the transfer is made in accordance with applicable data-protection law and, where required, is protected by an adequacy decision, appropriate contractual safeguards or another lawful transfer mechanism.

10. How long we keep personal data

Duevio retains personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it was collected and to satisfy applicable contractual, legal, accounting, security and regulatory requirements.

Enquiries and commercial discussions: may be retained for up to 24 months after the last meaningful interaction, unless a contractual relationship begins or continued retention is reasonably necessary.

Account and Subscription information: is retained for the duration of the relationship and thereafter for the period reasonably necessary to comply with applicable legal, accounting, taxation and limitation requirements.

Marketing information: is retained until consent is withdrawn or the information is otherwise no longer reasonably required for the marketing purpose.

Security and technical records: are retained for periods proportionate to security, fraud prevention, incident investigation and operational requirements, and may be retained longer where necessary in connection with a specific security incident or legal obligation.

Cookie and consent information is retained according to the applicable Cookie Policy and consent-management settings.

11. Cookies and similar technologies

Duevio uses cookies, local storage and similar technologies where necessary to operate the website and remember user preferences.

Non-essential analytics, advertising or similar technologies will be activated only where permitted by applicable law and, where required, after obtaining your consent.

Details of the technologies in use, their purposes and applicable retention periods are provided through the Cookie Policy and cookie preference centre.

You can change your non-essential cookie preferences at any time through the cookie settings available on the website.

12. Security

Duevio applies technical and organisational measures appropriate to the nature and risk of the personal data processed.

These measures include controls concerning secure transmission, authentication, access management, infrastructure security, monitoring, vulnerability management, backup and recovery.

No internet-based service can guarantee absolute security.

13. Automated decision-making

The Duevio website does not use personal data to make decisions based solely on automated processing which produce legal effects concerning you or similarly significantly affect you.

Where Duevio Customers use Platform functionality supporting screening, risk assessment or compliance decisions, the relevant Customer remains responsible for its own decision-making and applicable data-protection obligations.

  • withdraw consent where processing is based on consent; and
  • lodge a complaint with a competent supervisory authority.

These rights are not absolute and may be subject to conditions or exemptions under applicable law.

Requests may be sent to [email protected].

Duevio may take reasonable steps to verify your identity before acting on a request.

The Malta supervisory authority is the Office of the Information and Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC).

Duevio does not control the privacy practices of independent third-party services. You should review the applicable privacy information provided by those third parties.

AI Transparency

AI transparency and responsible use

Version: 24 August 2026

1. Scope

This notice describes the transparency principles Duevio should apply where an AI-assisted function is enabled. It does not state that every Duevio module uses AI and it does not classify any unverified function as high-risk.

2. Transparency at the point of use

Where an AI system is intended to interact directly with a natural person and the interaction is not obvious, the interface should clearly inform that person that they are interacting with an AI system, in line with Article 50 of the EU AI Act.

3. AI-generated or manipulated content

Where Duevio provides functions that generate or manipulate synthetic content, the provider and deployer responsibilities for machine-readable marking and user-facing disclosure should be assessed and implemented where Article 50 requires them.

4. Human oversight

AI-assisted outputs should be presented as support for qualified users. Compliance conclusions, customer risk decisions and regulatory actions require the organisation using Duevio to apply its own governance, policies and professional judgement.

5. AI literacy

Where Duevio personnel or customer personnel operate AI systems, the relevant provider or deployer should implement AI-literacy measures appropriate to the users' knowledge, experience and the context of use, as required by Article 4 of the EU AI Act.

6. Data protection

AI functionality that processes personal data remains subject to the GDPR. Controllers should assess lawful basis, transparency, data minimisation, security, retention, profiling and automated decision-making requirements before deployment.

7. Feature-specific assessment

Before any AI-assisted module is placed in production, its actual purpose, inputs, outputs, users and decision impact should be documented so the applicable role, risk classification and obligations under the AI Act can be determined from the real implementation.
